newsitem.title: UK: UK half-year business failures hit 7-year low- D&B.
newsitem.headline: UK half-year business failures hit 7-year low- D&B.

text.p: The number of firms going out of business in the UK in the first half of 1997 fell to 19,962, the lowest level since 1990, said business information specialists Dun & Bradstreet on Monday.
"These figures show that business failures are set on a downward trend," said D&B senior analyst Philip Mellor in a statement.
The number of companies to go to the wall was the lowest since the start of the last British recession in 1990 when 13,760 firms went under.
"We still have a long way to go before the business failure toll returns to pre-recessionary levels when there were less than 30,000 business failures a year," Mellor said.
At the height of the UK recession in 1993 D&B recorded 32,448 business failures in the first half of the year.
"The monthly toll of 3,000 plus is still far too high for comfort and companies need to look constantly over their shoulder at the viability of the firms with which they are doing business," he said.

The national average drop in business failures was 3.6 percent, compared with the first half of 1996. The East Midlands recorded a fall of 17.3 percent, the biggest drop in Britain but neighbouring West Midlands chalked up the biggest rise, at 13.7 percent.
Company liquidations across the UK fell by 8.8 percent but the picture was less bright for smaller firms, where business bankruptcies increased slightly by 0.6 percent, the survey said.

Business failures in London fell 3.5 percent to 3,124 from 3,236 during the equivalent period last year. London business failures accounted for 15.6 percent of the UK total. -- Nicholas Winning, London newsroom +44 171 542 7708
